newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog calls for cheap phones for all.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog calls for cheap phones for all.

text.p: UK telecoms watchdog Don Cruickshank said on Tuesday that everyone in Britain should be entitled to receive basic telephone services.
"A country which does not have its citizens connected to the telephone network is a country that is not fulfilling its potential," he said in a statement.
"It is also a country that is excluding some of its citizens from the social and economic opportunities which modern teleceoms services provide."

In a document called "Universal Telecommunications Services", Cruickshank said BT should provide cheap, "no frills" service packages to help connect the seven percent, or 900,000, of British homes which have no phones because they cannot afford it.
Dominant telecoms group British Telecommunications has agreed to reduce the numbers of disconnections for debt by offering help to customers in difficulty.

Cruickshank also wants special help for the elderly and disabled, such as a new BT "Lifeline" service this year, allowing customers to use a telephone for emergency and incoming calls only for 50 pence a week.
The regulator said that according to data provided by BT, no "undue net burden" would fall on the company by being a universal service provider.
No funding mechanism is therefore planned, although this will be reviewed in 1999, he said.
